text:
Lena: hey team, excited to start! hitting a weird stack of issues while bootstrapping my M2: dotfiles clone fails, asdf plugins missing, and GPG commit signing can't find my keyring. any quick hints?
Marco: welcome Lena! :wave: quick Qs: did you clone our dotfiles with SSH or HTTPS? corporate firewall sometimes blocks submodule fetches over HTTPS.
Lena: i cloned with HTTPS per the readme. `git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles.git` then `git submodule update --init --recursive` errors out on a private submodule with "unable to access".
Priya: if your laptop is on the corporate VPN/proxy, git might need the proxy set. Try `git config --global http.proxy http://proxy.corp:3128` (ask infra for proxy host). Or clone via SSH if you added your SSH key to GitHub.
Lena: i'm on home WiFi, not VPN. trying SSH clone gives permission denied (publickey). `ssh -T git@github.com` fails.
Marco: check `ssh-add -l` and `echo $SSH_AUTH_SOCK`. On mac, 1Password or Keychain can hold keys. Also check `~/.ssh/config` has `IdentityFile` pointing to the right key.
Lena: ssh-agent lists no identities. I imported the key into 1Password and enabled "allow SSH agent" there, but `ssh-add -l` still empty.
Priya: 1Password's agent exposes a socket; set SSH_AUTH_SOCK to it. Example: `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$(op-ssh-agent-socket)` or follow 1Password docs. For a quick workaround, run `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.
Lena: ok added key and SSH test works now. SSH clone succeeded. submodules still failing though: one submodule uses git+ssh url that points to a private repo on a corporate GitLab with a self-signed cert for package registry. `git submodule update` errors on SSL certificate verify.
Marco: if it's an internal cert, we add it to macOS trust store. Save the cert file and open it in Keychain Access, set to always trust. Then restart terminal. For Docker pulls to private registry you may also need to add the CA to `/etc/docker/certs.d/registry.corp:5000/ca.crt`.
Lena: added cert to Keychain, reran `git submodule update` and it progressed further. Now asdf: `asdf list` shows nothing and `node` command is system 20. I'm using fish shell (fish 3.6) so my dotfiles had fish config lines.
Priya: asdf support for fish requires adding init to `~/.config/fish/config.fish`:
```
source (brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.fish
```
and ensure `/opt/homebrew/bin` is in PATH for login shells. Fish doesn't read zsh files.
Lena: added the fish init, restarted fish, `asdf plugin-add nodejs` errors with gpg missing. `brew install gpg` fixed that. ran the node plugin import script and installed 18.16.0.
Marco: nice. last bit: GPG commit signing. `git commit -S` complains no secret key. I generated a subkey in GPG and uploaded the public key to GitHub, but gpg won't find the secret because gpg-agent socket differs between gpg2 and gpg1.
Priya: on mac, install `pinentry-mac` and configure `~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf` with `pinentry-program /opt/homebrew/bin/pinentry-mac` and `enable-ssh-support`. Then restart gpg-agent: `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent`. Also export GPG_TTY and set `echo 'export GPG_TTY=$(tty)' >> ~/.config/fish/config.fish` for fish.
Lena: did that; now `gpg --list-secret-keys` shows my key and `git commit -S` signs correctly.
Marco: pro tip: if your dotfiles have an `install.sh` that runs `asdf install --all`, run that once after plugins are added. For heavy repos, run with `--skip-existing` to avoid re-downloading.
Lena: ran install, most tools configured. only remaining oddity: VS Code says "certificate has expired" when connecting to our internal dev server from the Remote SSH extension.
Marco: Remote SSH uses the system OpenSSH and macOS trust store. Ensure the server cert is in Keychain and marked trusted for SSL, and your `~/.ssh/config` isn't forcing strict checks. If it's a server identity issue, add the host key with `ssh-keyscan` into `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.
Lena: added host key and cert trust; vscode remote connected. all green! thanks for the help.
Infra Bot: Hi Lena  welcome aboard! Docs: https://intranet.redwood/company/onboarding/dev-setup, internal CA guide: https://intranet.redwood/security/internal-ca, dotfiles repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles. If you need a proxy host or cert file, ping #eng-infra.
DevEx Bot: Nice work troubleshooting! If you'd like, run `curl -fsSL https://get.redwood.dev/bootstrap | bash` to reconcile common installs and open a deck issue in #devex for any recurring gap.
Lena: will do, really appreciate the quick responses :raised_hands:
